name.en-US: Bl. Ignatius de Azevedo and Companions
name.pt-BR: Beato Inácio de Azevedo e companheiros

prayerExcerpt.en-US: Grant us to profess steadfastly the faith we received from our forebears.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Concedei-nos professar constantemente a fé que recebemos de nossos antepassados.

meta.face: Inácio: a noble Portuguese priest of about forty-three with a BROAD, full, rounded-square face and wide cheekbones, a short straight nose, wide-set warm dark eyes under straight dark brows, a full mouth; THICK wavy dark-brown hair with a full hairline (not receding, not balding), and a FULL, ROUNDED dark-brown beard (not pointed, not a goatee); a steady, luminous upward gaze. He must look clearly different from St. Ignatius of Loyola (balding, lean, short pointed beard). The companion: a slender boy of about seventeen with a fresh, broad-cheeked face — a short, slightly upturned nose, large, clear light eyes under straight fair brows, a square, cleft chin and a wide, eager mouth; beardless, with short fair-brown hair and an ardent look.
meta.basis: In every known image Azevedo is bearded, to show his middle age against the extreme youth of nearly all his companions, and holds the Madonna of St. Luke, with a ship as the other obligatory attribute (Via Spiritus 2008). The youngest named companion, António Correia of Porto (1553–1570), was about seventeen.
